enumDescriptions: Plum and lavender, the hues of the cel-lens logo.
Warm browns and ambers, close to a plain YAML string.
No cel-lens colors; the theme alone colors the YAML.
cel-lens.colorStyle.markdownDescription: The color style for the parts of a CEL expression in Kubernetes YAML. Pick it from the status bar menu or with **cel-lens: Choose Color Style**.

cel-lens.inlineInfo.markdownDescription: Shows a line above each CEL rule: what `self` is, whether the rule compiles, and the values it reads as `dyn`. Turn it off and on with **cel-lens: Toggle Inline Info** or from the status bar menu.

cel-lens.exampleResults.markdownDescription: Shows what each rule of a CustomResourceDefinition does to the example objects of the workspace: a part of the line above the rule (such as `3 examples pass` or `refuses 1 example it should allow`), a section of its hover and a warning for each wrong verdict. Off, the engine reads, checks and runs no example. Turn it off and on with **cel-lens: Toggle Example Results** or from the status bar menu.

cel-lens.valueTypes.markdownDescription: Shows, in the line above a rule, the values the rule reads: each with its type or its *Give it a type*, *Edit* and *Remove* parts, and `+N more` when there are more than fit. Off, the line keeps its state and its example result, and the types you gave still apply. It only has an effect while the experimental feature `cellens-types` is on in `cel-lens.experimental`. Turn it off and on with **cel-lens: Toggle Value Types** or from the status bar menu.

cel-lens.kubernetesVersion.markdownDescription: Advanced: the Kubernetes version the results match, such as `1.36`. Leave empty to use the engine's default.

cel-lens.trace.server.markdownDescription: Traces the messages between VS Code and the engine in the cel-lens output channel.
enumDescriptions: Trace the messages without their contents.
Trace the messages with their contents.
Colors, checks, hovers and completes Kyverno ValidatingPolicy documents; experimental because compiled with Kyverno's compiler but never run against Kyverno's engine; only ValidatingPolicy is read.

Types the params, and the object and oldObject of a policy that matches a custom resource, from a CustomResourceDefinition found in the workspace, and hover says the feature is off when it is; experimental because the workspace scan runs only while the feature is on, at initialize or when the setting turns it on. It runs in the background and open documents are checked again when it ends. It reads at most 20000 YAML files and skips files over 1 MiB, so a CRD past either limit leaves its type dyn; the engine warns once at the file cap; a single skipped file is logged on its own line, and many are reported in one summary log line with their count, the limit and the first three names.

After a dot completion offers only what the receiver has, before a dot only the names of the document, and hover says why a value is dyn; experimental because built after v0.17.1 of the engine and not yet proven on real use.

Types the dyn values a .cellens file names, with completion, hover and problems as you edit it, and offers Give it a type on the line above a rule; off, no .cellens is read, those values stay dyn and hover says the feature is off; experimental because the types are yours: nothing checks them against a cluster.

cel-lens.experimental.markdownDescription: Advanced: the experimental features to turn on, such as `cellens-types`, which reads your `.cellens` files and offers **Give it a type**. An experimental feature is off until you list it here; a name the engine does not know is ignored and reported once in a notification.

cel-lens.serverPath.markdownDescription: Advanced: path to a `cel-lens-core` binary to use instead of the engine bundled with the extension. Leave empty.

cel-lens.ruleView.followEditor.markdownDescription: Selects, in the cel-lens view, the rule the cursor is in, a moment after the cursor moves. It never takes the focus and never opens the view. Turn it off and on with **Stop Following** and **Follow Editor** in the view's title menu.

walkthroughs.title: Get started with cel-lens
walkthroughs.description: Check the CEL rules of your Kubernetes YAML as you type.

steps.title: Open a sample CRD
steps.description:
A CustomResourceDefinition with four CEL rules, kept in the extension's own storage, never in your workspace. cel-lens colors each rule, and the line above it says what self is and whether the rule compiles.
[Open the Sample CRD](command:cel-lens.openSample)

media.altText: A rule of the sample CRD in the editor, colored, with the line above it: self: Widget.spec · compiles.

steps.title: See a problem and fix it
steps.description:
One rule reads self.replica, a field the schema does not have, and cel-lens underlines it. The quick fix list offers **Change to `replicas`** first: pick it, and the problem is gone.
[Fix the Problem](command:cel-lens.fixSampleProblem)

media.altText: The rule self.replica > 0 with replica underlined as an error, and the quick fix list below it with Change to replicas first.

steps.title: Pick the Kubernetes version
steps.description:
The status bar item shows the Kubernetes version the results match, such as CEL · K8s 1.36. Click it for its menu, which has every setting and toggle of cel-lens.
[Pick Kubernetes Version](command:cel-lens.pickKubernetesVersion)

media.altText: The Kubernetes version picker listing 1.36 as the current version above older ones, and the status bar item CEL · K8s 1.36.

steps.title: Choose the colors
steps.description:
cel-lens colors the parts of each rule in one of three styles: CEL, Classic or Off. **Toggle Colors** and the status bar menu turn them off and on again.
[Choose Color Style](command:cel-lens.chooseColorStyle)

media.altText: The color style picker listing CEL, the current style, then Classic and Off.

scripts.bench: esbuild src/*.bench.ts --bundle --platform=node --format=esm --alias:vscode=./test/vscode.ts --outdir=out/bench --out-extension:.js=.mjs --log-level=warning && for f in out/bench/*.mjs; do node --expose-gc $f || exit 1; done
scripts.e2e: npm run engine && vitest run --config vitest.e2e.config.mts
